families.family_description: OH-rich biopolymer films combined with retained acid and 1-D confining fillers target bound-fluid proton pathways that remain connected in the cold window.
descriptor_match: D2: plasticised or retained polar phase is supported by DES/chitosan evidence and preferred for low-temperature use
D3: polysaccharide/PVA-like hosts are analogously flexible hydrogen-bonded films rather than brittle dry solids
D4: phosphoric-acid or DES-based proton carriers are supported as non-neat acid forms
D5: starch/chitosan plus 1-D clay or nanotube fillers support confined interconnected channels
D6: starch, PVA, chitosan, and phosphoric acid provide dense hydrogen-bond relay sites
D7: chitosan, attapulgite, halloysite, and low-level PA strategies support retention

families.family_description: Polymer hosts embedding acid-complexing eutectic phases aim to suppress crystallisation and preserve a mobile hydrogen-bonded conducting fraction at low temperature.
descriptor_match: D2: DES incorporation is directly linked to bound/plasticised polar-fluid continuity
D4: ChCl/PA and DES claims support cold-stable complexed acid speciation
D6: polymer OH/NH groups plus acid/eutectic species provide relay-rich hydrogen-bond networks
D7: chitosan-containing DES films show retention without disintegration

families.family_description: Amorphous phosphate-rich networks offer intrinsically continuous proton pathways with strong internal hydrogen-bonding and confinement-like retention.
descriptor_match: D1: phosphate glass is directly described as an amorphous continuous proton-transport medium
D6: phosphate glass provides strong proton-associated hydrogen-bond environments
D7: protonated phosphate networks inherently retain the conducting phase, albeit conditionally in some reports

instances.composition_description: A quaternary film using chitosan as the acid-retaining biopolymer, PVA as the flexible OH-rich film former, attapulgite as a 1-D confining filler, and phosphoric acid as the proton source.
expected_properties: cold_window: plausible bound-acid continuity under confinement
nanoconfinement: 1-D filler may maintain connected proton channels
mechanical: PVA/chitosan blend should reduce brittle channel disconnection
risk_flags: PA leaching if acid loading is excessive
cold performance is inferred by analogy rather than directly reported

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is supported as an acid-interacting scaffold that retains conducting phase and tolerates hydrated/plasticised loading.
PVA contributes an OH-rich hydrogen-bonding film matrix analogous to relay-supporting flexible blends.
1-D attapulgite is directly supported for channel guidance, nanoconfinement, and acid immobilisation.
Phosphoric acid is supported as a complexable proton source and as a hydrogen-bond-mediated proton-conducting phase.

instances.novelty_rationale: This follows the requested low-temperature synergy motif by combining a biopolymer host, PVA-like film former, 1-D clay, and phosphoric acid. The exact four-part formulation is not present in the claim pool, but each element has directly relevant support.

instances.composition_description: A starch–PVA blend membrane loaded with phosphoric acid and halloysite nanotubes to confine the acid in an OH-rich flexible matrix.
expected_properties: cold_window: bound-water and acid continuity are plausible in the OH-rich blend
retention: HNT confinement should reduce phosphoric-acid loss
transport: starch/PVA hydrogen-bond density may support hybrid proton hopping
risk_flags: starch-rich films may swell under high water uptake

element_evidence.reason: Starch is supported as an OH-rich channel-forming phase with dense hydrogen-bond functionality.
PVA adds OH-mediated hydrogen-bond connectivity and blend compatibility.
HNTs are directly supported as nanoconfining hosts that reduce PA leaching.
PA is supported as the proton source, relay medium, and a species whose retention can improve at controlled loading.

instances.novelty_rationale: The blend merges starch/PVA hydrogen-bonding with halloysite PA confinement, a supported but not directly claimed combination. It is novel as a cross-paper assembly aimed specifically at the 182–299 K window.

instances.composition_description: A chitosan membrane incorporating a choline chloride–phosphoric acid eutectic-like proton phase retained within the biopolymer.
expected_properties: cold_window: eutectic acid complex may resist crystallisation better than neat acid/water
retention: chitosan should hold the conductive phase without collapse
conductivity: mixed vehicular and hydrogen-bond relay transport is plausible
risk_flags: DES viscosity may limit mobility at the low end of the window
water balance may strongly affect performance

element_evidence.reason: Chitosan is supported for retaining hydrated or acid-like conductive phases without structural failure.
ChCl is directly supported as the complexing counter-species in ChCl/PA deep eutectic formation.
PA is directly supported as the acid component of the eutectic and as a hydrogen-bond-mediated proton conductor.

instances.novelty_rationale: The claim pool supports chitosan with DES generally and ChCl/PA eutectics separately, but not this exact membrane formulation. The novelty is the targeted integration of a cold-stable acid complex into a retention-capable biopolymer host.

instances.composition_description: An amorphous protonated phosphate glass network used as a control inorganic proton conductor with no added polymer or liquid acid phase.
components: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)
expected_properties: pathway: amorphous continuous proton-transport medium is directly supported
retention: conducting phase is intrinsically immobilised within the network
thermal: no freezing transition of a separate aqueous phase is expected
risk_flags: cold-range conductivity is not directly reported in the pool
long-term proton-conductivity stability can be conditional

element_evidence.component: phosphate glass (APS proton-substituted / protonated phosphate network)
element_evidence.reason: The phosphate glass network is directly reported as amorphous, proton-conducting, hydrogen-bond-supporting, and retaining the protonic phase within the glass.

instances.novelty_rationale: This exact-match control is retained because it directly satisfies the continuity-centered inorganic archetype from the literature. It provides a non-polymeric benchmark against which colder, plasticised candidates can be compared.

instances.composition_description: A mixed biopolymer composite where starch and chitosan host phosphotungstic acid around a 1-D attapulgite network for retained proton relay.
expected_properties: nanoconfinement: attapulgite should organize interconnected acid-bearing pathways
relay_density: PWA plus polysaccharide functionalities may provide strong proton-transfer sites
retention: chitosan and filler may suppress heteropolyacid migration
risk_flags: heteropolyacid humidity dependence may complicate low-temperature transport

element_evidence.reason: Starch is supported as a hydrogen-bond-dense channel-forming polysaccharide.
Chitosan is supported as a percolated acid-interacting scaffold with retention capability.
Attapulgite is directly supported for 1-D channel guidance and acid immobilisation.
PWA is directly supported as a dense proton-relay species that can be immobilized in composites.

instances.novelty_rationale: This candidate extends the supported chitosan–attapulgite–acid motif by adding starch as a second OH-rich host to tune bound-water and channel continuity. The exact starch/chitosan/attapulgite/PWA combination is not claimed in the pool, making it a plausible novel assembly.
